P0200.title: Injector Circuit/Open
P0200.description: P0200 is the injector circuit fault without a cylinder assignment. The large US manufacturers do not use it – GM and Ford report injector faults per cylinder (P0201 ff) or as faults of the shared injector supply (P062D/P062E, P2146 ff). Saab documents it on the 3.0 V6 diesel of the 9-5, whose injectors are driven by a separate power stage behind the glovebox: there P0200 means an electrical fault in that power stage or its wiring, and the engine is shut down. Generally the cause lies in something all injectors share – supply, fuse, relay, ground or driver stage – so several cylinders are affected at once. CARB does not require separate codes for each kind of circuit fault.

causes.label: Shared injector supply open (fuse, relay, harness connector)
Separate injector power stage or its wiring faulty (diesel)
Driver stage in the engine module faulty
Ground fault of the module or power stage

symptoms: Engine does not start or shuts down

P0201.title: Cylinder 1 Injector A Circuit/Open
P0201.description: P0201 reports an electrical fault, mainly an open circuit, in the injector circuit of cylinder 1. The engine module watches each injector output: GM flags an open circuit at an impedance of 200 kΩ or more – on direct injection and diesel engines in 10 of 20 or 5 of 10 samples and with the warning light in the first trip, on some port-injected engines only after two trips. Ford's port injection reads a fault bit from the driver chip that covers open, short to ground and short to voltage alike; Ford diesels report only the open circuit here and shorts as P0261/P0262. On direct injection the affected injector is switched off; the cylinder misfires.

causes.label: Connector at the cylinder 1 injector loose, corroded or with a broken or pushed-back pin
Injector coil open
Wire between module and injector open or chafed (heat, rodents)
Injector supply missing (fuse, relay) – then usually several cylinders at once
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Misfire and rough running, misfire code P0301
Limp mode possible on diesel and direct injection

P020A.title: Cylinder 1 Injection Timing
P020A.description: P020A reports a fault in the injection timing of cylinder 1 on a diesel engine. Unlike P01CB/P01CC ('over retarded/advanced', the result of the injector learning routine in overrun), this code has no direction, and what it checks is up to the manufacturer. GM uses it as an electrical check on a four-cylinder diesel and on the 6.6 litre L5P Duramax V8: at every injection the engine module measures how long the injector current takes to reach its pull-in level of 13 A. If on the V8 that time is outside 60–150 µs in 10 of 20 samples, the code sets and the warning light comes on in the first trip. FCA lists it for the 3.0 litre EcoDiesel V6 together with the learning codes: check injector coding, charge air leaks and the injector clamp, reset the zero fuel calibration and repeat the learning drive; if the code returns, the injector is replaced.

causes.label: Injector of cylinder 1 faulty (coil, armature, wear, deposits)
Injector wiring or connector: contact resistance, corrosion, chafing
Engine software sets the code falsely (update available for some models)
Injector driver stage or boost voltage in the engine module
Wrong injector code, contaminated fuel or loose injector clamp

symptoms: Rough running or misfire, rough idle
Loss of power, smoke or knocking possible

P0213.title: Cold Start Injector 1
P0213.description: A cold start injector is an additional injector in the intake manifold that sprays extra fuel for a few seconds while a cold engine is cranked. In classic Bosch systems a thermo-time switch on the block powers it directly, without the engine module – such systems cannot set a code at all. A code is only possible where the engine module drives the valve and monitors its circuit, as CARB requires for output components. From the 1990s the main injectors took over cold-start enrichment, so the code only fits early OBD II engines. P0213 concerns cold start injector 1. No manufacturer using it was found in GM, Ford or Saab documents.

causes.label: Connector or wire corroded or open
Valve coil open or valve stuck
Thermo-time switch or control relay faulty
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Poor cold start, long cranking in cold weather
Leaking valve: hot-start problems, flooding, black smoke

P0215.title: Engine Shutoff Solenoid
P0215.description: The engine shutoff solenoid is the electric stop valve on older diesel injection pumps, mainly distributor pumps. It is energised with the ignition on and lets fuel into the pump; with no current a spring closes it, the pump runs dry and the engine stops – also as a safety backup if the governor fails. P0215 reports a fault in this solenoid or its supply, typically a broken coil, a sticking plunger, a blown fuse or relay, or a wiring fault. The result is either an engine that will not start or dies, or one that keeps running after switch-off. Newer diesels stop through the injectors or a fuel shutoff valve with its own codes P0005–P0007. No manufacturer document describing P0215 was found; the description rests on CARB's requirements for output components and a Bosch patent on the valve.

causes.label: Shutoff solenoid faulty (open coil, sticking plunger)
Relay or fuse in the supply circuit faulty
Broken wire, corrosion or ground fault at the pump connector
Pump control module faulty
Engine module driver faulty

symptoms: Engine does not start or stalls while driving
Engine keeps running after ignition off (solenoid stuck open)

P0216.title: Injector/Injection Timing Control Circuit
P0216.description: P0216 is a diesel code for the control of injection timing. On 1990s distributor pumps with an electronic timing advance it meant that actual injection timing missed its target; today manufacturers use it for the electronic injector control, with different meanings. GM's Duramax diesels compare, inside the engine module, the summed injection pulse widths from the hardware driver with those calculated by the software; a mismatch in 30 of 124 or 60 consecutive checks sets the code with the warning light in the first trip. On GM's 3.0 litre LM2 it appeared together with P0202 from a broken pin in the injector 2 connector. Saab's 3.0 V6 diesel uses it for a fault in the separate injector power stage. The result can be loss of power, rough running, smoke and limp mode.

causes.label: Injector harness or connector (broken pin) – common rail
Engine module or injector power stage faulty internally
Distributor pump electronics or timing advance faulty
Low supply pressure on distributor pumps (lift pump, filter)
Pump installed incorrectly, drive gear misaligned

symptoms: Hard starting or stalling (distributor pump), smoke

P0217.title: Engine Coolant Over Temperature Condition
P0217.description: P0217 is a condition code: the engine module reports that coolant temperature has passed a protection threshold. The limit and the reaction depend on the manufacturer – Saab's 2.2 diesel sets it at 120 °C for over 10 s, limits fuel quantity and suspends EGR and boost diagnostics until the temperature drops; heavy-duty diesels cut power sharply and may shut down; Ford petrol engines use their own code P1299 and cut fuel to individual cylinders. Whether the warning light comes on varies, because CARB exempts overheat protection that only engages once the gauge reads red. Usual causes are low coolant, a thermostat stuck closed, a failed fan or water pump – but Ford traced some cases to a faulty coolant sensor or harness.

causes.label: Low coolant (leak, head gasket)
Thermostat stuck closed
Radiator fan, fan clutch or water pump faulty, radiator clogged
Coolant temperature sensor or harness faulty (false reading)
Extreme load (towing, gradient, heat) with an intact cooling system

symptoms: Temperature gauge in the red, overheat warning
Loss of power, limp mode, cylinders possibly shut off
Steam or coolant smell, coolant loss

P0218.title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor A Over Temperature Condition
P0218.description: P0218 is a condition code: the transmission or engine module reports that transmission fluid temperature sensor A reads above an overheat limit. Saab's Aisin automatic sets it above 170 °C for more than 10 s, or above 140 °C for two minutes at high speed, shows a 'transmission overheating' warning and shifts less smoothly; afterwards a fluid change is advised because the additives are spent. Ford uses its own code on diesels and lists P0218 without the warning light on other models. Reactions include earlier torque converter lock-up, a modified shift pattern and sometimes reduced power. Causes are real overheating – towing, hills, low or old fluid, a clogged cooler – or a sensor reading wrongly.

causes.label: High load (towing, hills, sustained full throttle, stop-and-go in heat)
Transmission fluid low or aged
Fluid cooler, thermostat or lines clogged, weak cooling system
Torque converter clutch slipping or internal damage
Temperature sensor or wiring reading wrongly

symptoms: Limp mode or reduced power possible

P0219.title: Engine Overspeed Condition
P0219.description: P0219 is a condition code: engine speed has exceeded the overspeed limit even though the rev limiter already cuts fuel – so the engine was driven from outside, usually by downshifting at too high a road speed or descending in too low a gear, or the speed signal was wrong. Limits: Ford 6.7 litre diesel above 4,200 rpm, 3.0 litre above 4,800 rpm, after 0.1 s; GM/Saab 2.8 V6 petrol with manual gearbox above 7,000 rpm for 1 s; Saab 2.2 diesel above 6,200 rpm, although fuel is cut from 5,000 rpm. Many manufacturers store it without the warning light. Saab advises: together with a camshaft sensor code it was real overspeed, alone check the speed signal; after real overspeed inspect the engine for valve train damage.

causes.label: Downshift at too high a road speed (manual gearbox)
Descending in too low a gear
Fault in the speed signal (crankshaft sensor, wiring)
Diesel runaway (oil drawn into the intake) or sticking injection

symptoms: Usually no lasting symptoms, only a stored code
Briefly very high revs, limiter intervening
After real overspeed: rattling, loss of power

P0220.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit

P0225.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch C Circuit

Wiring or connector (supply, signal line)
5 V reference disturbed
Engine module

P0226.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch C Circuit Range/Performance

P022A.title: Charge Air Cooler Bypass Control A Circuit/Open

P0230.title: Fuel Pump Primary Circuit
P0230.description: The fuel pump circuit has two sides: the primary circuit is the engine module's output to the fuel pump relay coil (or to a pump control module), the secondary circuit is the power circuit from relay contact or module to the pump itself. P0230 concerns the primary side. GM's output driver compares the commanded with the actual state of the relay control circuit and sets the code at 8 of 10 mismatches, after two trips; Ford checks for open or short circuits for 2–5 s. With a failed relay control the pump stays off and the engine will not start or dies; a short to voltage keeps the pump running and drains the battery. On Ford systems with a pump control module the code means its power relay circuit; on the Subaru-based Saab 9-2X it is the pump module's collective fault report.

causes.label: Fuel pump relay faulty (coil open or shorted)
Control wire from module to relay open or shorted to ground or voltage
Relay supply, ground or fuse missing
With a pump control module: its supply, ground or the module itself
Engine module driver faulty

symptoms: Engine cranks but does not start
No pump prime noise at ignition on; with a short to voltage the pump runs on and drains the battery

P0231.title: Fuel Pump Secondary Circuit Low
P0231.description: The fuel pump circuit has two sides: the primary circuit is the engine module's output to the fuel pump relay coil (or to a pump control module), the secondary circuit is the power circuit from relay contact or module to the pump itself. P0231 means the secondary side reads low, and the meaning differs by system. The pump gets no voltage, so the engine will not start or stalls.

P0232.title: Fuel Pump Secondary Circuit High

P0234.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger A Overboost Condition
P0234.description: P0234 is a function code, not a sensor fault: the engine module compares target and actual boost, and actual boost stays above target although the control is already lowering it (wastegate opened, variable vanes opened). P0235.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor A Circuit
P0235.description: Boost sensor A measures the absolute pressure between charge air cooler and throttle – GM calls it TIAP, Ford TIP – usually combined with an intake air temperature sensor; its voltage rises with pressure. P0238.description: Boost sensor A measures the absolute pressure between charge air cooler and throttle – GM calls it TIAP, Ford TIP – usually combined with an intake air temperature sensor; its voltage rises with pressure. P0238 means the signal voltage is above its upper limit: GM above 86 % of 5 V (about 372 kPa) for roughly 4 s with the warning light in the first trip, Ford above 4.88 V for 5 s, Saab's 1.6 turbo above 4.8 V. Causes are a signal shorted to 5 V or 12 V, an open sensor ground or – on GM modules with a pull-up input – an open signal wire. If several high codes appear at once, check the shared ground. With a sensor fault boost control is switched off and only the base boost of the wastegate spring remains, with a clear loss of power.

causes.label: Sensor ground open, or signal wire open on a pulled-up input
Signal shorted to 5 V or 12 V
Sensor faulty internally
Connector corrosion or moisture at the ground
Engine module

symptoms: Clear loss of power, only base boost
Boost reading implausible in a scan tool

P0239.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor B Circuit
P0239.description: Boost sensor B is a second boost pressure sensor, for a second turbo or bank on parallel twin-turbo engines or a second stage on two-stage systems. No manufacturer using sensor B codes was found – GM, Ford and Saab, even on two-stage and twin-turbo engines, use a single boost sensor; the description follows CARB and the documented sensor A codes. P0239 is the general circuit fault of sensor B, the counterpart of P0235, without telling low, high or range apart. As with sensor A, boost control would be switched off, with loss of power.

causes.label: Connector or wire to sensor B open or corroded
Sensor B faulty or oily
Shared 5 V reference or ground disturbed
Engine module

symptoms: Uneven boost build-up on twin turbos

P023A.title: Charge Air Cooler Coolant Pump A Control Circuit/Open
P023A.description: Some engines cool the charge air with a coolant-to-air cooler in its own low-temperature circuit, driven by an electric pump – GM uses this on supercharged V8s such as the LT4 (Camaro ZL1, Corvette Z06, CTS-V) and LT5 (Corvette ZR1). P023A means GM's driver diagnosis has found an open circuit (more than 200 kΩ between output and ground with the low-side driver off). Bundled conditions: main relay at least 11 V, ignition above 5 V; 50 of 63 samples set the code with the warning light in the first trip on 2018–2019 engines, older modules need two trips. Without the pump the charge air gets hot and boost is limited.

causes.label: Wire or connector at the pump open (front area, corrosion)
Pump faulty (motor or electronics)
Fuse, pump relay or supply missing
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Loss of power under load or in heat (boost limited)

P023B.title: Charge Air Cooler Coolant Pump A Control Circuit Low
P023B.description: Some engines cool the charge air with a coolant-to-air cooler in its own low-temperature circuit, driven by an electric pump – GM uses this on supercharged V8s such as the LT4 (Camaro ZL1, Corvette Z06, CTS-V) and LT5 (Corvette ZR1). P023B means GM's driver diagnosis has found a short to ground (0.5 Ω or less between output and ground with the driver off). Bundled conditions: main relay at least 11 V, ignition above 5 V; 50 of 63 samples set the code with the warning light in the first trip on 2018–2019 engines, older modules need two trips. Without the pump the charge air gets hot and boost is limited.

causes.label: Control wire to the pump shorted to ground
Pump shorted internally
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Loss of power under load or in heat (boost limited)

P023C.title: Charge Air Cooler Coolant Pump A Control Circuit High
P023C.description: Some engines cool the charge air with a coolant-to-air cooler in its own low-temperature circuit, driven by an electric pump – GM uses this on supercharged V8s such as the LT4 (Camaro ZL1, Corvette Z06, CTS-V) and LT5 (Corvette ZR1). P023C means GM's driver diagnosis has found a short to voltage (0.5 Ω or less between output and battery voltage with the driver on). Bundled conditions: main relay at least 11 V, ignition above 5 V; 50 of 63 samples set the code with the warning light in the first trip on 2018–2019 engines, older modules need two trips. Without the pump the charge air gets hot and boost is limited.

causes.label: Control wire to the pump shorted to voltage
Pump shorted internally (overcurrent)
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Loss of power under load or in heat (boost limited)

P023D.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure - Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor A Correlation
P023D.description: P023D compares the manifold pressure sensor (after the throttle) with boost sensor A (before the throttle): with the engine stopped both must read the same ambient pressure. Saab's 2.8 V6 checks this once per trip with the ignition on before starting and sets the code at a difference of more than 12 kPa, with the warning light and limp mode limited to 170 Nm. The code does not say which sensor is wrong – barometric pressure as a third value decides. Electrical faults of either sensor (P0107/P0108, P0237/P0238) block the test and must be fixed first. GM and Ford run the same comparison but report it as P0236, P0106 or P2227.

causes.label: Manifold or boost sensor drifting or dirty
Contact resistance at connector or ground of one sensor
Pressure port or hose of one sensor blocked (oil sludge, ice)
Engine module or reference voltage

P023E.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure - Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor B Correlation
P023E.description: Boost sensor B is a second boost pressure sensor, for a second turbo or bank on parallel twin-turbo engines or a second stage on two-stage systems. No manufacturer using sensor B codes was found – GM, Ford and Saab, even on two-stage and twin-turbo engines, use a single boost sensor; the description follows CARB and the documented sensor A codes. P023E is the counterpart of P023D: manifold pressure is compared with boost sensor B, and with the engine stopped both must read ambient pressure. Saab sets the sensor A version at a difference of more than 12 kPa; a deviation beyond the manufacturer's limit sets this code.

causes.label: Boost sensor B or manifold sensor drifting
Contact resistance at sensor B's connector or wire
Pressure port blocked

P023F.title: Fuel Pump Secondary Circuit/Open
P023F.description: The fuel pump circuit has two sides: the primary circuit is the engine module's output to the fuel pump relay coil (or to a pump control module), the secondary circuit is the power circuit from relay contact or module to the pump itself. P023F means the power circuit to the pump is open. GM pumps with their own power module, whose speed is controlled by rail pressure, measure the pump current: if it stays below 1 A (older modules 0.5 A) although the pump is commanded, the code sets with the warning light in the first trip, and fuel pressure diagnostics are suspended. The cause lies in the wire from module to pump or its return, the pump connector or the pump motor itself. The pump stops, so the engine will not start or dies – there is no limp mode.

causes.label: Pump connector at tank flange or pump module open or corroded
Fuel pump open internally (brushes, winding)
Wire from module to pump or return wire open
Pump control module faulty

symptoms: Engine does not start, no pump noise

P0240.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P0240.description: Boost sensor B is a second boost pressure sensor, for a second turbo or bank on parallel twin-turbo engines or a second stage on two-stage systems. No manufacturer using sensor B codes was found – GM, Ford and Saab, even on two-stage and twin-turbo engines, use a single boost sensor; the description follows CARB and the documented sensor A codes. P0240 is the plausibility fault of sensor B with an electrically valid signal – as with sensor A, compared with barometric and manifold pressure after a stop and with a model while running. A charge air leak on the side or stage of turbo B is a likely cause.

causes.label: Charge air leak on the side or stage of turbo B
Sensor B dirty or drifting
Contact resistance in the connector
Manifold or barometric sensor faulty

P0241.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor B Circuit Low
P0241.description: Boost sensor B is a second boost pressure sensor, for a second turbo or bank on parallel twin-turbo engines or a second stage on two-stage systems. No manufacturer using sensor B codes was found – GM, Ford and Saab, even on two-stage and twin-turbo engines, use a single boost sensor; the description follows CARB and the documented sensor A codes. P0241 means the signal of sensor B is below its lower limit – for sensor A, GM uses 14.4 % of 5 V and Ford 0.19 V for 5 s. Causes are a short to ground, an open 5 V reference or a failed sensor.

causes.label: Signal or 5 V reference wire open or shorted to ground
Connector unplugged or corroded
Sensor faulty internally
5 V reference pulled down by another sensor

symptoms: Boost B reads very low in a scan tool

P0242.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor B Circuit High
P0242.description: Boost sensor B is a second boost pressure sensor, for a second turbo or bank on parallel twin-turbo engines or a second stage on two-stage systems. No manufacturer using sensor B codes was found – GM, Ford and Saab, even on two-stage and twin-turbo engines, use a single boost sensor; the description follows CARB and the documented sensor A codes. P0242 means the signal of sensor B is above its upper limit – for sensor A, GM uses 86 % of 5 V and Ford 4.88 V for 5 s. Causes are a short to voltage, an open ground or, on a pulled-up input, an open signal wire.

causes.label: Sensor ground open, or signal wire open on a pulled-up input
Signal shorted to 5 V or 12 V
Sensor faulty internally
Engine module

symptoms: Boost B shows its maximum value

P0243.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate Actuator A
P0243.description: The wastegate lets exhaust bypass the turbine to limit boost; actuator A is either a pulse-width-modulated solenoid on a pneumatic wastegate can or an electric actuator with a position sensor. P0243 is the general circuit fault of actuator A. GM uses it for an open circuit: with the driver off, more than 200 kΩ between output and ground in 10 of 20 samples sets it with the warning light in the first trip (older modules: two trips). Ford uses P0243 on its electric wastegates as the collective code for open and short circuits (0.4 s), together with P2ABD for driver overcurrent or overheating. Boost control is then switched off and only the spring-set base boost remains – less power, but no risk of overboost.

causes.label: Connector at the wastegate valve or actuator loose, corroded or with spread contacts
Valve coil or electric actuator winding open
Supply voltage to the valve missing (ignition, relay, fuse)
Broken control wire between module and valve
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Clearly less power, boost only at base level

P0244.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate Actuator A Range/Performance
P0244.description: The wastegate lets exhaust bypass the turbine to limit boost; actuator A is either a pulse-width-modulated solenoid on a pneumatic wastegate can or an electric actuator with a position sensor. P0244 means the actuator does not respond as commanded although its circuit is electrically sound, and manufacturers implement it differently. Subaru engines (Saab 9-2X) set it when manifold pressure exceeds an altitude-dependent limit – about 220 kPa absolute at sea level – for over 2 s, with the warning light at once. Stellantis documented it with a wastegate rod that had come off for want of a retaining clip. Older GM modules (Saab LDK, LLU) however use P0244 for an open solenoid circuit; newer GM and Ford systems do not use it and monitor function under P0234/P0299 or P25B3/P25B4.

causes.label: Wastegate rod unhooked, retaining clip missing or linkage worn
Wastegate flap coked or sticking
Control hose to the wastegate can leaking, off or swapped; diaphragm torn
Wastegate solenoid mechanically stuck
Position sensor of the electric actuator not learned correctly

symptoms: Lack of power or surging, too high boost
Rattle or whistle at the turbo possible

P0245.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate Actuator A Low
P0245.description: The wastegate lets exhaust bypass the turbine to limit boost; actuator A is either a pulse-width-modulated solenoid on a pneumatic wastegate can or an electric actuator with a position sensor. P0245 means the control circuit of actuator A reads low – typically the ground-switched control wire shorted to ground, so the valve would be permanently energised. GM checks with the driver off for less than 0.5 Ω to ground, 10 of 20 samples, warning light in the first trip; Ford's driver chip reports it after 2–5 s, and on pneumatic wastegates Ford also includes the open circuit here. A shorted supply shared with the bypass valve can set it together with P0033/P0034. Boost control is then switched off and only the spring-set base boost remains – less power, but no risk of overboost.

causes.label: Control wire to the wastegate valve chafed through to ground
Solenoid shorted internally
Shared supply shorted (e.g. by the bypass valve)
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Clearly less power, boost only at base level

P0246.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate Actuator A High
P0246.description: The wastegate lets exhaust bypass the turbine to limit boost; actuator A is either a pulse-width-modulated solenoid on a pneumatic wastegate can or an electric actuator with a position sensor. P0246 means the control circuit of actuator A reads high – the control wire is shorted to voltage, so the driver cannot switch the valve to ground. GM checks with the driver on for less than 0.5 Ω to battery voltage, 10 of 20 samples, warning light in the first trip; Ford's driver chip reports it after 2–5 s, and Ford's functional check of the wastegate control pressure (P1015/P1016) only runs when P0245/P0246 are clear. Boost control is then switched off and only the spring-set base boost remains – less power, but no risk of overboost.

causes.label: Control wire touching voltage (damaged harness, neighbouring wire)
Solenoid shorted internally (very low resistance, driver overcurrent)
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Clearly less power, boost only at base level

P0247.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate Actuator B
P0247.description: The wastegate lets exhaust bypass the turbine to limit boost; actuator B is either a pulse-width-modulated solenoid on a pneumatic wastegate can or an electric actuator with a position sensor. B is the second turbo or actuator, so B codes only exist on engines with two. P0247 is the general circuit fault of actuator B, the counterpart of P0243. On GM's 3.0 litre twin-turbo V6 (LGW) it means an open circuit of more than 200 kΩ with the driver off, 10 of 20 samples, warning light in the first trip. Ford uses it on twin-turbo V6 engines with electric wastegates as the collective code for open and short circuits (0.4 s), together with P2ABE. Boost control on that side is switched off, costing power.

causes.label: Connector at wastegate valve or actuator B loose or corroded
Coil or motor winding of actuator B open
Broken control or supply wire
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Clearly less power, boost only at base level

P0248.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate Actuator B Range/Performance
P0248.description: The wastegate lets exhaust bypass the turbine to limit boost; actuator B is either a pulse-width-modulated solenoid on a pneumatic wastegate can or an electric actuator with a position sensor. B is the second turbo or actuator, so B codes only exist on engines with two. P0248 is the counterpart of P0244: actuator B does not reach the commanded position, or boost does not respond as expected, although the circuit is electrically sound. Stellantis documents it on the 2025 Ram 1500 with the 3.0 litre Hurricane twin-turbo, often with P2B94 (position sensor B learning limit): incorrectly fitted retaining clips on the wastegate rod caused missing turbo boost. Thresholds are not published; GM and Ford do not use the code, Ford monitors actuator B position under P25B5/P25B6.

causes.label: Retaining clip of the wastegate rod missing or fitted wrongly, rod unhooked
Wastegate flap B coked or sticking
Position sensor learned value outside limits (e.g. not relearned after turbo replacement)
Pneumatic wastegate: control hose or can B leaking

symptoms: Missing turbo boost, lack of power

P0249.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate Actuator B Low
P0249.description: The wastegate lets exhaust bypass the turbine to limit boost; actuator B is either a pulse-width-modulated solenoid on a pneumatic wastegate can or an electric actuator with a position sensor. B is the second turbo or actuator, so B codes only exist on engines with two. P0249 means the control circuit of actuator B reads low, typically the control wire shorted to ground. On GM's LGW twin-turbo less than 0.5 Ω to ground with the driver off in 10 of 20 samples sets it with the warning light in the first trip; older GM modules need two trips. Ford reports it on pneumatic wastegates after 2–3 s. Boost control is then switched off and only the spring-set base boost remains – less power, but no risk of overboost.

causes.label: Control wire of wastegate B chafed through to ground
Valve or actuator winding B shorted
Connector damage or moisture
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Clearly less power, boost only at base level

P024A.title: Charge Air Cooler Bypass Control A Range/Performance
P024A.description: The charge air cooler bypass is a flap or valve that routes compressed air around the charge air cooler, so the engine and exhaust warm up faster after a cold start; when warm it closes or opens partly to control intake air temperature. It is driven by an electric motor with a built-in position sensor or by a solenoid and vacuum can. P024A is the functional fault: the bypass does not follow its command, judged from the position sensor or from the expected temperature effect – Bosch describes comparing the cooler's efficiency with the valve closed and open, using modelled air temperature before and measured temperature after the cooler. FCA documents P024A, together with P026E, on the 2017 Alfa Romeo Giulia and 2018 Stelvio with the 2.0 turbo and fixed it with an engine software update, so check the software level first.

causes.label: Bypass flap sticking, coked or oily (oil from crankcase ventilation or turbo)
Actuator weak or vacuum line leaking
Engine software (FCA 2.0 turbo)
Position sensor inaccurate or connector corroded

symptoms: Longer warm-up or higher charge air temperature
Possibly less power from boost limitation

P024B.title: Charge Air Cooler Bypass Control A Stuck
P024B.description: The charge air cooler bypass is a flap or valve that routes compressed air around the charge air cooler, so the engine and exhaust warm up faster after a cold start; when warm it closes or opens partly to control intake air temperature. It is driven by an electric motor with a built-in position sensor or by a solenoid and vacuum can. P024B means the bypass flap does not move at all despite being commanded – the position signal stands still or the air temperature shows no reaction. Bosch's patent describes exactly the case of a valve stuck closed or a blocked bypass, which raises emissions during warm-up. Stuck open, the charge air gets hotter and power drops; stuck closed, warm-up takes longer. No manufacturer document using this code was found – GM and Ford do not use the bypass codes; the description rests on CARB's component monitoring requirement and a Bosch patent on the bypass valve.

causes.label: Flap seized or coked
Actuator faulty (gear, motor)
Vacuum supply missing (pneumatic type)
Position sensor reading constant

symptoms: Stuck open: higher charge air temperature, loss of power

P024C.title: Charge Air Cooler Bypass Position Sensor A Circuit
P024C.description: The charge air cooler bypass is a flap or valve that routes compressed air around the charge air cooler, so the engine and exhaust warm up faster after a cold start; when warm it closes or opens partly to control intake air temperature. It is driven by an electric motor with a built-in position sensor or by a solenoid and vacuum can. Its position sensor is usually built into the actuator, with a 5 V reference and a ratiometric signal. P024C is the general circuit fault of the position sensor, for manufacturers that do not split low and high. Bypass control is then switched off and the flap stays in its rest position. No manufacturer document using this code was found – GM and Ford do not use the bypass codes; the description rests on CARB's component monitoring requirement and a Bosch patent on the bypass valve.

causes.label: Connector or wiring to the actuator's sensor part
Built-in position sensor faulty
5 V reference disturbed by another sensor
Engine module

symptoms: Depending on the rest position: longer warm-up or higher charge air temperature with slight loss of power

P024D.title: Charge Air Cooler Bypass Position Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P024D.description: The charge air cooler bypass is a flap or valve that routes compressed air around the charge air cooler, so the engine and exhaust warm up faster after a cold start; when warm it closes or opens partly to control intake air temperature. It is driven by an electric motor with a built-in position sensor or by a solenoid and vacuum can. Its position sensor is usually built into the actuator, with a 5 V reference and a ratiometric signal. P024D is the plausibility fault: the signal is electrically valid but does not match the commanded position or the end stops. Bypass control is then switched off and the flap stays in its rest position. No manufacturer document using this code was found – GM and Ford do not use the bypass codes; the description rests on CARB's component monitoring requirement and a Bosch patent on the bypass valve.

causes.label: Flap or linkage misadjusted or sticking
Sensor drifting or track worn
Contact resistance at the connector
End stops not learned after replacement

symptoms: Depending on the rest position: longer warm-up or higher charge air temperature with slight loss of power

P024E.title: Charge Air Cooler Bypass Position Sensor A Circuit Low
P024E.description: The charge air cooler bypass is a flap or valve that routes compressed air around the charge air cooler, so the engine and exhaust warm up faster after a cold start; when warm it closes or opens partly to control intake air temperature. It is driven by an electric motor with a built-in position sensor or by a solenoid and vacuum can. Its position sensor is usually built into the actuator, with a 5 V reference and a ratiometric signal. P024E means the signal is below its lower limit – a signal wire shorted to ground or an open signal or 5 V reference wire. Bypass control is then switched off and the flap stays in its rest position. No manufacturer document using this code was found – GM and Ford do not use the bypass codes; the description rests on CARB's component monitoring requirement and a Bosch patent on the bypass valve.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to ground or open
5 V reference missing
Sensor faulty
Connector corroded

symptoms: Depending on the rest position: longer warm-up or higher charge air temperature with slight loss of power

P024F.title: Charge Air Cooler Bypass Position Sensor A Circuit High
P024F.description: The charge air cooler bypass is a flap or valve that routes compressed air around the charge air cooler, so the engine and exhaust warm up faster after a cold start; when warm it closes or opens partly to control intake air temperature. It is driven by an electric motor with a built-in position sensor or by a solenoid and vacuum can. Its position sensor is usually built into the actuator, with a 5 V reference and a ratiometric signal. P024F means the signal is above its upper limit – typically an open sensor ground or a signal shorted to voltage. Bypass control is then switched off and the flap stays in its rest position. No manufacturer document using this code was found – GM and Ford do not use the bypass codes; the description rests on CARB's component monitoring requirement and a Bosch patent on the bypass valve.

causes.label: Sensor ground open
Signal shorted to 5 V or system voltage
Sensor faulty
Connector corroded

symptoms: Depending on the rest position: longer warm-up or higher charge air temperature with slight loss of power

P0250.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate Actuator B High
P0250.description: The wastegate lets exhaust bypass the turbine to limit boost; actuator B is either a pulse-width-modulated solenoid on a pneumatic wastegate can or an electric actuator with a position sensor. B is the second turbo or actuator, so B codes only exist on engines with two. P0250 means the control circuit of actuator B reads high: the control wire is shorted to voltage, checked with the driver on. GM's LGW twin-turbo sets it at less than 0.5 Ω to battery voltage in 10 of 20 samples with the warning light in the first trip; older GM modules need two trips. Ford reports it on pneumatic wastegates after 2–3 s. Valve B can no longer be controlled, so that side runs on base boost.

causes.label: Control wire of wastegate B shorted to voltage
Winding shorted internally (overcurrent)
Connector corroded or damp
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Clearly less power, boost only at base level

P0251.title: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control A (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0251.description: These codes cover the electrically controlled fuel metering actuator on a diesel injection pump. On older distributor pumps it was a solenoid that set the injected quantity; on common rail it is usually an inlet metering valve on the high-pressure pump that lets only as much fuel into the pumping elements as the rail needs, instead of spilling the excess through a pressure valve. Manufacturers use different codes for this part: Ford P0001–P0004, GM Duramax P0090–P0092. P0251 is the general circuit fault of actuator A. Saab's 2011 9-5 diesel uses it for an open circuit of the pressure regulator on the high-pressure pump: if the control wire does not show the expected voltage with the driver off for more than 1 s, the code sets with the warning light at once. Depending on the system, rail pressure and power are then limited.

causes.label: Metering actuator coil open
Connector at the actuator corroded or loose, broken wire
Supply voltage to the actuator missing
Distributor pump: internal electronics or quantity valve faulty
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

P0252.title: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control A Range/Performance (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0252.description: These codes cover the electrically controlled fuel metering actuator on a diesel injection pump. On older distributor pumps it was a solenoid that set the injected quantity; on common rail it is usually an inlet metering valve on the high-pressure pump that lets only as much fuel into the pumping elements as the rail needs, instead of spilling the excess through a pressure valve. Manufacturers use different codes for this part: Ford P0001–P0004, GM Duramax P0090–P0092. P0252 is the range or performance fault of actuator A, and the meaning depends on the maker. Saab's 2011 9-5 diesel sets it when the driver stage of the pump pressure regulator overheats – a sign of a shorted turn or excessive current – with the warning light at once; Ford checks the same under P0002 at a driver temperature above 170 °C. Generally the code can also mean the actuator does not achieve the expected effect.

causes.label: Metering actuator with shorted turns, too low resistance (driver overheats)
Actuator mechanically sticking or dirty (fuel quality, wear debris)
Wiring with contact resistance
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

P0253.title: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control A Low (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0253.description: These codes cover the electrically controlled fuel metering actuator on a diesel injection pump – on common rail usually an inlet metering valve on the high-pressure pump that sets how much fuel is compressed. P0253 means the actuator A circuit reads low. Saab's 2011 9-5 diesel uses it for a control wire shorted to ground for more than 1 s, with the warning light at once. Saab's 3.0 V6 diesel, whose pump has two metering valves, also includes an open circuit (over 2.1 s) and goes into limp mode: limited pedal response and injection quantity, rail pressure capped at 60 MPa, warning light if the fault recurs on the next trip. Ford's equivalent is P0003, GM's P0091.

causes.label: Control wire to the metering actuator chafed to ground
Connector or wire open (where makers include it under low)
Metering actuator faulty internally
Engine module faulty

symptoms: Limp mode with limited power and speed

P0254.title: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control A High (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0254.description: These codes cover the electrically controlled fuel metering actuator on a diesel injection pump – on common rail usually an inlet metering valve on the high-pressure pump that sets how much fuel is compressed. P0254 means the actuator A circuit reads high or draws too much current – typically the control wire shorted to voltage. Saab's 2011 9-5 diesel sets it after 1 s with the warning light at once. On Saab's 3.0 V6 diesel a short to voltage of more than 0.31 s stops the engine, because a permanently energised valve can no longer control quantity and pressure. Ford's equivalent P0004 sets above 3.7 A; GM uses P0092.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to voltage
Metering valve with shorted turns (overcurrent)
Connector corrosion with leakage current
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Engine stalls or will not start (Saab 3.0 diesel)

P0255.title: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control A Intermittent (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0255.description: These codes cover the electrically controlled fuel metering actuator on a diesel injection pump – on common rail usually an inlet metering valve on the high-pressure pump that sets how much fuel is compressed. P0255 reports brief open or short circuits in the actuator A circuit that come and go – typically a loose contact or a wire breaking under vibration. No manufacturer using it with exactly this meaning was found; a Ram 6.7 Cummins code list names it as a circuit performance fault instead. The description follows CARB's continuous circuit monitoring requirement and the documented A siblings.

causes.label: Loose contact or corrosion at the metering actuator connector
Harness chafing intermittently (vibration)
Actuator coil with a temperature-dependent fault
Engine module

symptoms: Check engine light (often goes out again)

P0256.title: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control B (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0256.description: These codes cover the electrically controlled fuel metering actuator on a diesel injection pump – on common rail usually an inlet metering valve on the high-pressure pump that sets how much fuel is compressed. Actuator B is a second metering actuator, for example on pumps with two metering valves such as on Saab's 3.0 V6 diesel. P0256 is its general circuit fault, the counterpart of P0251. No manufacturer using P0256 was found – Saab reports its two valves under other codes; the description follows CARB's circuit monitoring requirement and the A siblings.

causes.label: Metering valve B open
Connector or wire to valve B open
Engine module

P0257.title: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control B Range/Performance (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0257.description: These codes cover the electrically controlled fuel metering actuator on a diesel injection pump – on common rail usually an inlet metering valve on the high-pressure pump that sets how much fuel is compressed. P0257 is the functional fault of actuator B: the metering does not achieve its target. Engine power may be derated.

Poor low-pressure supply (filter, lift pump, air)
Metering actuator or pumping element worn
Software or diagnostic level

symptoms: Hard starting, low rail pressure when cranking

P0258.title: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control B Low (Cam/Rotor/Injector)

P0258 means the actuator B circuit reads low. Connector at the pump corroded or loose
Metering valve shorted to ground internally
Engine module

symptoms: Check engine light on (after the second trip)
Raised idle speed in limp mode

P0259.title: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control B High (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0259.description: Fuel metering actuator B is a second electrically controlled metering valve on a diesel injection pump; A has the codes P0251–P0255. P0259 means its circuit reads high or draws too much current – a short to voltage or a shorted turn. GM and Ford use other codes for this part (P0090–P0092, P0001–P0004).

causes.label: Metering valve B shorted internally
Control wire to the valve shorted to voltage, chafing
Connector at the valve corroded or wet
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Limp mode with limited power and speed

P025A.title: Fuel Pump Module A Control Circuit/Open
P025A.description: On demand-controlled fuel systems the engine module does not drive the pump itself but sends a pump control module the desired pump output on a separate control line, usually as a duty cycle; the module reports back on a monitor line or via CAN. P025A means the control line from the engine module to pump module A is open or faulty. On Ford systems the pump module itself detects the bad command signal and reports it on the monitor line (11–16 V, 2–5 s); Ford uses P025A for the shared line to modules A and B. GM's pump module compares the enable line with the request on the data bus and sets P025A after about 1 s, with the warning light in the first trip; on some Ford vehicles the code does not light it.

causes.label: Control line to the pump module open or shorted, often along the frame
Connector at the pump module corroded or wet (module often mounted on the frame)
Pump control module faulty (input)
Module ground or supply poor
Engine module output faulty

symptoms: Lack of power from wrong fuel pressure

P025B.title: Fuel Pump Module A Control Circuit Range/Performance
P025B.description: On demand-controlled fuel systems the engine module does not drive the pump itself but sends a pump control module the desired pump output on a separate control line, usually as a duty cycle; the module reports back on a monitor line or via CAN. causes.label: Contact resistance or corrosion in the control line or connector distorting the duty cycle
Pump control module faulty
Interference or poor ground between engine module and pump module
Engine module software or output

symptoms: Lack of power from wrong fuel pressure

P025C.title: Fuel Pump Module A Control Circuit Low

causes.label: Control line chafed to ground at the frame
Water or corrosion at the pump module connector
Ground point loose or corroded
Pump control module faulty internally
Pump relay faulty (Ford 6.7)

symptoms: Loss of power from low supply pressure

P025D.title: Fuel Pump Module A Control Circuit High

causes.label: Control line shorted to battery voltage or another wire
Moisture in the connector (leakage to voltage)
Pump control module faulty
Relay stuck or faulty (Ford 6.7)

symptoms: Pump runs all the time or not at all

P025E.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor A Intermittent/Erratic
P025E.description: Boost sensor A measures the pressure between charge air cooler and throttle (Ford TIP, GM TIAP). P025E counts brief excursions outside its valid voltage range that are each too short for the low or high code P0237/P0238 – Ford's limits are below 0.19 V and above 4.88 V. causes.label: Loose contact or corrosion at the sensor connector
Wire or 5 V reference breaking from vibration or heat
Sensor faulty internally (erratic signal)
Shared 5 V reference disturbed by another sensor

symptoms: Occasional loss of power, boost limited

P025F.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor B Intermittent/Erratic

No manufacturer using sensor B codes was found; the description follows CARB's input monitoring requirement and Ford's sensor A check.

causes.label: Loose contact or corrosion at the sensor B connector
Wire breaking from vibration or heat
Sensor B faulty

P0260.title: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control B Intermittent (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0260.description: P0260 reports brief dropouts or jumps in the circuit of fuel metering actuator B on a diesel injection pump that do not last long enough for the low or high code (P0258/P0259) – typically a loose contact or a wire breaking under vibration. Broken or chafed wire in the harness to the pump (vibration, heat)
Metering valve B with internal dropouts
Unstable supply or ground

P0261.title: Cylinder 1 Injector A Circuit Low

Injector shorted to its housing internally
Open control wire (on some GM port-injection drivers this also reads low; P020x sets too)
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

symptoms: Misfire and rough running, misfire code P0301
Injector shut off, limp mode possible on diesels

Short between supply and control wire in harness or connector
Driver stage in the engine module faulty

P0263.title: Cylinder 1 Contribution/Balance

The code sets when the correction for cylinder 1 reaches its limit and the cylinder still does not keep up – GM at 95 % of a limit of about ±12–17 mm³ for 30 s, Ford above 90 % of the allowed 3.5–15 mg per stroke for 7.5 s; GM needs two trips. Engine software outdated or diagnosis too sensitive
Injector correction codes not or wrongly programmed after replacement
Low compression on cylinder 1 (valve, rings, injector seal)
Crankshaft sensor or tone wheel learning faulty, dual-mass flywheel

P026A.title: Charge Air Cooler Efficiency Below Threshold
P026A.description: P026A means the charge air cooler is not cooling enough. The module compares the temperature drop across the cooler with the maximum possible (inlet minus ambient) or with a model: GM's 6.6 litre LML diesel sets it below 25 % efficiency, later GM diesels below 50 %, both after two trips; Ford's 6.7 and 3.0 diesels when the measured temperature is 18–35 °C (3.0: 35–65 °C) off the model over about 10 s. symptoms: Loss of power under load or in heat

P026B.title: Injection Timing Performance

It is documented on the Ram 6.7 Cummins, together with the per-cylinder timing and balance codes; FCA describes it as set falsely by software and fixes it with an engine module update, without publishing thresholds. GM and Ford handle timing with per-cylinder codes instead (P01CB ff, P2B11 ff).

causes.label: Engine module software (false setting)
Injectors coked or worn (changed start of injection)
Rail pressure or fuel supply problems (pump, filter, fuel quality)
Crankshaft or camshaft signal inaccurate

symptoms: Possibly knocking, rough running or more smoke

P026C.title: Fuel Injection Quantity A Lower Than Expected
P026C.description: From 2010, CARB requires diesel engines to detect when the commanded injection quantity is not delivered. The module estimates the fuel actually burned from airflow and the measured lambda (from the NOx or oxygen sensor) and corrects the quantity; if that correction passes a limit, the code sets. P026C means the engine gets less fuel than commanded. GM's 6.6 litre LML diesel checks it at idle with the vehicle stationary and the engine warm, setting it at a correction of −20 to −35 mm³ per stroke for 12 s; later GM diesels use the learned correction value (10 of 20 samples); both need two trips. FCA lists it with an injector cleaning procedure for deposits. Ford diesels do not use it. Typical causes are coked injectors, wrong airflow or lambda measurement and weak fuel supply.

causes.label: Injectors coked or clogged (too little flow)
Airflow or boost measurement wrong, NOx sensor lambda inaccurate
Weak low- or high-pressure supply (filter, pump, rail pressure)
Fuel quality or contamination
Software

P026D.title: Fuel Injection Quantity A Higher Than Expected

P026D means the engine gets more fuel than commanded. GM's LML diesel sets it at idle at a correction of +16 to +35 mm³ per stroke for 12 s, two trips. On GM's 2.8 litre diesel vans of 2020–2022 it could also be a software anomaly without driving problems. Symptoms are black smoke and more frequent filter regeneration.

causes.label: Injector dripping or worn, or wrong injector type fitted
EGR valve not closing or EGR differential pressure sensor wrong
Boost sensor or turbo vanes faulty, intake leak
NOx or oxygen sensor reading wrong
Software

symptoms: Black smoke, higher soot load, more frequent filter regeneration

P026E.title: Charge Air Cooler Coolant Pump A Performance
P026E.description: Some engines cool the charge air with a coolant-to-air cooler in its own low-temperature circuit with an electric pump. FCA documents it on the 2017 Alfa Romeo Giulia and 2018 Stelvio with the 2.0 turbo, together with P024A, and fixed it with a software update; thresholds are not published. causes.label: Air in the low-temperature circuit or low coolant (pump runs dry)
Pump faulty internally (bearing, impeller, electronics)
Software or calibration
Weak supply or ground, corroded connector

symptoms: Loss of power in heat or under load
Level in the auxiliary coolant tank drops

P026F.title: Coolant Thermostat Performance

No manufacturer using P026F was found – GM and Ford report thermostat faults as P0128, P01F0 or P2181 – so the description rests on CARB and the thermostat's function.

causes.label: Thermostat stuck open or opening too early

Map-controlled thermostat: heating element or control faulty
Coolant temperature sensor inaccurate
Low coolant or air in the system

P029A.title: Cylinder 1 - Fuel Trim at Max Limit

Injector circuit high-resistance or connector
Petrol: false air at this cylinder's intake (manifold gasket)
Injector correction code missing or wrong after replacement

P02CC.title: Cylinder 1 Fuel Injector A Offset Learning At Min Limit

P02CC means the learned correction for cylinder 1 has reached its lower limit at at least one pressure step: the injector needs much less activation time than nominal – it delivers too much at small quantities or opens early. GM diesels set it at limits of roughly ±66–182 µs after two trips. It is documented on GM's 6.6 litre L5P and 2.8 litre diesels – on the 2.8 a worn drive belt caused it to return after injector replacement – and on Land Rover's 5.0 V8 petrol, where a software update is the first step. It differs from P01CC (over advanced), which some systems derive from the same learning.

causes.label: Injector of cylinder 1 leaking or over-delivering at small quantities
Engine software (update available for some models)
Injector correction code not or wrongly programmed after replacement
Disturbed crankshaft signal (worn drive belt, tone wheel, dual-mass flywheel)

symptoms: Often nothing noticeable; possibly rough idle or knocking

P02CF means the learned correction for cylinder 2 has reached its upper limit at at least one pressure step: the injector needs much more activation time than nominal – it delivers too little or opens late, for example from coking. It is documented on GM's 6.6 litre L5P and 2.8 litre diesels – on the 2.8 a worn drive belt caused it to return after injector replacement – and on Land Rover's 5.0 V8 petrol, where a software update is the first step. It differs from P01CD (over retarded), which some systems derive from the same learning.

P02E0.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control Circuit/Open
P02E0.description: The diesel intake air flow valve A is the throttle flap ahead of the intake manifold of a diesel engine: it creates the vacuum needed for high EGR rates, lowers airflow to heat the particulate filter and catalyst during regeneration and closes at switch-off against run-on shaking. A spring holds it open when unpowered; an electric motor positions it, with a position sensor reporting back. P02E0 means the motor circuit is open – cable, connector or motor winding. GM diesels detect more than 200 kΩ with the driver off, after about 1.5 s (6.6 litre LML: 7 s), two trips. On a fault the valve is switched off and the spring opens it: driving is usually little affected, but EGR control is restricted and filter regeneration may be blocked.

causes.label: Connector at the throttle corroded or loose
Broken motor wire
Motor winding of the valve open
Driver stage in the engine module

symptoms: Filter regeneration does not run, soot load rises

P02EA.description: The diesel intake air flow valve A is the throttle flap ahead of the intake manifold of a diesel engine: it creates the vacuum needed for high EGR rates, lowers airflow to heat the particulate filter and catalyst during regeneration and closes at switch-off against run-on shaking. A spring holds it open when unpowered; an electric motor positions it, with a position sensor reporting back. P02EA reports brief dropouts or jumps of the position signal – loose contacts, a wire breaking under movement or faulty digital sensor messages. No manufacturer using P02EA was found – GM reports such faults under its own codes, Ford does not use it – so the description follows CARB's input monitoring requirement. On a fault the valve is switched off and the spring opens it: driving is usually little affected, but EGR control is restricted and filter regeneration may be blocked.

causes.label: Loose contact at connector or pins
Wire breaking under movement
Sensor with dropouts
Electromagnetic interference

P02EC.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control System - High Air Flow Detected

P02EE.title: Cylinder 1 Injector Circuit Range/Performance

The injector may be shut off, causing misfire.

causes.label: Injector electrically aged (piezo capacitance, coil resistance)

Injector mechanically sticking (valve lift)
Injector driver stage in the engine module

P02FA.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow Position Sensor Minimum/Maximum Stop Performance
P02FA.description: The diesel intake throttle learns the position sensor values of its end stops, as a Toyota patent describes for the closed stop at engine stop. P02FA means a learned end-stop value is implausible. Ford's 6.7 and 3.0 diesels check it once after each learning run and set the code when the learned minimum offset is outside ±10 (6.7) or ±6.7 (3.0) – Ford only evaluates the minimum stop. Typical causes are soot and oil deposits at the flap and stop, a worn or shifted sensor, mechanical damage or a replacement part that has not been learned. EGR control may be restricted.

causes.label: Soot and oil deposits at flap and stop (EGR, crankcase ventilation)
Position sensor in the throttle unit worn or shifted
Flap or shaft bent, stop worn, gear worn
Wrong or not learned replacement part
Engine software

symptoms: EGR control restricted, filter regeneration hindered

P02FB.title: Cold Start Fuel Injection Control Circuit/Open
P02FB.description: Cold start fuel injection is an extra injection system for cold starts – for example on flex-fuel engines running on high ethanol blends, where a Hyundai patent describes a small auxiliary tank, a cold-start injector and a heater. CARB lists such heated fuel preparation systems among the monitored output components. P02FB means the control circuit of the cold-start injection is open or has a general fault – a broken coil, a loose or corroded connector or a broken wire. The engine then starts poorly or not at all in the cold; once warm it runs normally. No manufacturer document using this code was found; unlike the older P0213/P0214, these codes separate the fault types.

causes.label: Coil of the cold-start injector or valve open
Connector loose, corroded or pin pushed back
Broken wire in the harness
Fuse or relay of the cold-start system
Driver stage in the engine module

symptoms: Hard or no start in cold weather (especially with high ethanol)
Rough running right after a cold start

P02FC.title: Cold Start Fuel Injection Control Circuit Low
P02FC.description: Cold start fuel injection is an extra injection system for cold starts – for example on flex-fuel engines running on high ethanol blends, where a Hyundai patent describes a small auxiliary tank, a cold-start injector and a heater. CARB lists such heated fuel preparation systems among the monitored output components. P02FC means the control circuit reads low – typically the control wire shorted to ground or a shorted turn in the cold-start injector. Depending on the circuit the valve then does not work, or it stays open and over-fuels the engine, causing fuel smell and hot-start problems. No manufacturer document using this code was found; unlike the older P0213/P0214, these codes separate the fault types.

causes.label: Control wire chafed through, shorted to ground
Shorted turn in the cold-start injector or valve
Water or corrosion in the connector
Driver stage in the engine module

symptoms: Hard cold start, or over-fuelling with fuel smell if the valve stays open

causes.label: Control wire shorted to a supply wire (chafed or pinched)
Short in the cold-start injector or valve

P02FF.title: Propulsion System Inactive Timer Performance
P02FF.description: Many diagnostics need to know how long the engine – or, on hybrids, the whole propulsion system – has been off: thermostat and evaporative checks and the cold-start strategy, for which CARB requires at least 6 hours of standstill. A timer measures this time, and the engine module checks its plausibility, for example against coolant cooling – a GM patent describes such a check. P02FF means that timer is implausible. Mercedes documents it on M256, M260, M264 and M274 engines of around 2020: after an internal reset the instrument cluster clock ran wrong; the fix is a software update for engine, transmission and instrument cluster modules. Readiness of standstill-dependent monitors may stay incomplete.

causes.label: Time source in another module (instrument cluster, body module) gives an implausible time after a reset or voltage loss
Software level of engine, transmission or instrument cluster module
Battery discharged or disconnected, voltage dips
Instrument cluster or timer in the engine module faulty
Coolant temperature sensor distorting the cooling check

symptoms: Check engine light on, otherwise usually nothing noticeable
Clock in the instrument cluster wrong or reset
